title: Standard Model particle identifications
purpose: Identify all 17 elementary particle types on one frozen candidate. Each species has a local preparation or production channel, reproducible detection statistics, and a dictionary that distinguishes its nearest alternatives. A declaration of a field or an input mass cannot identify the excitation.
reference: Count six quark flavours, three charged leptons, three active neutrino flavour channels, four gauge-boson types and the Higgs. W covers both signs, and the gluon entry covers the eight colour components. Resolve conjugate partners where distinct. Neutrino flavour is defined by weak production and detection; its propagation can mix mass eigenstates. Composite hadrons provide evidence for confined quarks and gluons. The hypothetical graviton has its own gravitational-particle assessment. A sterile neutrino is outside this inventory.

e.note: Two independent sources and two detectors identify the same charged winding state in free flight and at one resolved energy. Its contact charge is signed, its addressed winding rotation is orbital, and its clock line depends on the guide. A separate spinor shell requires repeated monitoring of prepared material heads. Intrinsic electron spin, electric flux and physical rest mass remain open. The lowest propagating band carries the winding code near a common guide threshold of 16 native units. After free flight a single negative charge carries three coherent winding amplitudes. Independent local phase and arm conventions reproduce ninety complete source and receiver banks. The conjugate windings have identical energy spectra. One terminal instrument couples each of the three arriving winding states to the same net-neutral pair, records donor compensation, and preserves the unknown winding. The full pulse gives conditional Schmidt-number-three fidelity lower bounds above 0.733 for both charge signs. A joint audit binds charge, recoil, winding, and stationary current to the same three lengths. It finds an idle enclosing boundary, orbital dispersion, and zero stationary bond current on the isolated lines. In the matched exchange test, vacancy centres move and the winding labels stay at the original hubs.

comparison.label: Screened flux in a separate signed-load construction
comparison.finding: The ring extension has a signed material load and a screened field measurable 22 cells away. The hard-core orbital is identified by its route, applied coupling and detector. The ordered exchange can leave its orbital state behind. Physical electron spin, exchange and an independently calibrated rest energy on the same excitation remain open. On the asymmetric 320-cell four-fan path a finite coherent clock and a local charge-and-ring measurement retain source-reference entanglement at every free wait. A positive distant ring can occur on over 98% of a selected input’s rare terminal coincidences. The measured energy beat changes with length. A signed terminal load and one local triangle certify entanglement with a fresh source reference after three contacts and no intermediate reports. On copies of that same arrival two head reads give opposite field currents for the two reference-Y records, and a reciprocal material probe at two and three hops responds to a phase change at fixed initial sharp word and charge probabilities. Holding the source and probe gives zero connected near-far energy difference. Only 0.80646% of the sharp late arrivals pass a subsequent two-line energy test. The separately prepared local clock measures a length-dependent formation-line spacing, and a collision-free cycle interchange leaves a distinguishable bridge record. A local balanced split on these arrivals has equal formation mean under native and half-rate bridges and independently measured different recoil. An addressed circuit restores the face and reference record with a positive orbital return. Resolved forward and reverse material circuits can each return the reference-tagged triangle. The isolated native triangle has zero stationary material current for every scalar port trap. A supplied full-cell head completion and fifty-five addressed swaps also give a positive return after five exact proper-pose checkpoints with the charge arrested at the hub. A completed three-arm junction at 1045 now realizes collision-free exchange of two material loads with all 36 written heads restored and a positive matched phase. Both independent field correlations remain at their original sites. Open-junction free returns distinguish the polarized fermion comparator, while the spin singlet exactly reproduces the native spatial generator. A distinct native-pulse route on the 1045–1028 junction exchanges both material origins and both independently referenced physical face codes with positive SWAP phase. Complete local attachment is verified at the endpoints. The earlier material-only route leaves both field references parked. A supplied 48-owner route from the 1045 vacancy gate measures an extended formation line and independently counted recoil and drift. The measured midband and held-drift enclosures exclude a common massive speed on that band. A localized electron mass remains unresolved. The finite-pin collar on the same 1045 herald resolves a selected near/far spectral contrast that vanishes in the ideal clamp. Exact inverse-square suppression in pin strength and the port-symmetry polarity control restrict its interpretation as an electric force. On a 1047 five-face wheel, five native transfers of both late 1045 face words give opposite reference-conditioned stationary material currents on a selected energy line and distinct exterior-head probe probabilities. Physical magnetic and angular-momentum calibration remain open. Each of ten charge-and-incident-face detector pairs on the five rim sites certifies entanglement with the original reference on this same stationary line. The prespecified 1046 reader admits 0.00774461% per original launch and its nine-setting simulation gives a simultaneous 99% witness interval of [−0.009898, −0.009566]. For ideal opposite-current sources at wait four, the exterior-head contrast starts at cubic order in the exterior contact rate η and the probability of leaving the original energy-line and exterior-word subspace is at most 64η². Whole-cell head changes on the same signed arrival have the measured discrete divergence and fail the finite Green circulation test at all enrolled native waits and in the uniform face-randomization limit. One calibrated outside head reads the stationary five-face material current, and three settings of that same head certify the late reference correlation. The complete native exchange orbit imposes a nonzero inclusive bright floor on an equal coherent input, and the signed whole-cell Gauss sector excludes every proper half-turn. A positive detector resolves the compensated pole on the extended vacancy route. Exact same-sector arithmetic excludes a beat at that rest frequency, while three held small wave numbers agree with the independently calibrated expansion through the tested quartic allowance. One admitted negative 1045 arrival passes a rest-line measurement, returns through a native guide-head and wheel handoff, and then gives stationary material-current and reference records. After the finite filter, inverse calibrated rest preparation and the sharp origin herald reject every orthogonal guide line exactly and act by one scalar on both arriving face words and their reference. The full sequence admits 1.17509e−5 per original launch. The late exterior/reference simultaneous 99% interval is [−0.01175134,−0.00594249]. The two outside-current intervals conditional on the reference are [−0.04933091,−0.04707781] and [0.01007460,0.01262901]. This measures a selected extended guide line and a stationary wheel current on one sequence with a supplied filter, guide and aperture.

mu.note: Three mobile bound cores have incompatible rest and recoil hierarchies. A separate localized charged orbital demonstrably loses one native unit as a stocked neutral pair gains one unit in another owner. The emitting orbital lacks a physical muon mass and weak-flavor tag. The eight periodic guides with a common positive light threshold miss at least one of the two laboratory ratios by 29.2% or more across every triple of band minima. Every matched-host formation energy of the three-arm doublet apparatus lies between 8 and 27, excluding the laboratory hierarchy throughout that sector. On a twelve-port native vacancy, a common periodic drive produces three resolved clock rates. Their ratios approach 1, 206.770316 and 3477.472837 in the weak-drive limit at the programmed register phase. All three encoded states couple out during unforced evolution.

nu-e.note: At full conversion all 2,493,659 neutral detections resolve opposite charges on the two measured ports. A remote observer can compare joint signed arrivals after free flight on the prepared route. A calibrated negative or positive weak daughter sorts the neutral inputs of the declared exterior doublet. An explicit pair of charged constituents gives exactly the same total gauge currents as the direct doublet. An independently identified charged partner at production and detection is still needed for a flavour assignment. At two distant receivers, an inverse native ladder gives a signed daughter and a compensating donor read on the same projected neutral arrival. The two material orders respond to opposite fixed analyzer settings. A remote clock and signed coincidence on a driven neutral pair resolve energies near 49 and 50 on its filled guide. This source excludes a light pair in its charge sector and supplies no flavour identification. After free neutral release, the same local three-port receiver distinguishes three addressed-arm preparations. Measured source-direction weights and four calibrated transport responses explain the three distributions. The two conjugate winding inputs have exactly the same remote readout.

families.name: Quarks
families.criterion: Recover the spin-half colour-triplet sector, its electric and weak responses, and a flavour discriminator in colour-singlet production, decay or scattering records. Resolve the conjugate sector.
types: Distinguish strangeness from light down flavour.
Identify charm production or weak transitions separately from up.
Resolve the heavy up-type resonance and its weak decay.

families.name: Charged leptons
families.criterion: Resolve spin half, unit negative charge, colour neutrality and weak interactions. Discriminate the three generations and their positive-charge conjugates through spectral or decay measurements.
types: Distinct mass and leptonic decay channel.
Third charged-lepton branch, with its weak decay channels.

families.name: Active neutrinos
families.criterion: Resolve a neutral spin-half weak sector, tag flavour by the accompanying charged lepton, and relate production, propagation and detection with the same mixing dictionary. Distinguish neutrino and antineutrino interaction channels where measurable.

families.name: Gauge bosons
families.criterion: Identify polarization, charge and the current coupled to the same propagating vector excitation.
types: Massless transverse electromagnetic response and its coupling to the measured electric current.
Colour-octet strong-current response and non-Abelian couplings in gauge-invariant signals.
Both signs of the massive charged weak vector and charged-current transitions.
Massive neutral weak vector, its polarizations and neutral-current couplings.

families.name: Scalar boson
families.criterion: Identify a neutral spin-zero resonance with independently distinguished couplings in the same electroweak sector.
types: Electroweak symmetry-breaking scalar and its characteristic production or decay responses.
